_meta.denominator: team games in every season the player appeared on a ROSTER, so a fully missed season counts against him. Counting only seasons with a stat line would skip a lost year entirely and report the player as durable.

gates.note: a one-season sample is a fact about one year; calling it a rate implies a trend. Practice-squad and cut seasons are excluded, and the population is limited to players who held a real role at some point — without that gate the league-wide median came out at 25%, which measures roster churn rather than durability

_meta.hierarchy_rank: 2 — opportunity. It is the volume multiplier every per-game rate in this app silently assumes.
_meta.not_medical: This cannot separate injury from a coaching decision, a suspension or a holdout. The player was off the field; the reason is not in this data.
_meta.not_role: This blends availability with ROLE, because the gameday inactive list is unavailable. A backup who dresses every week and never plays scores low, which is correct for fantasy and is not a statement about his health. Read it beside snap share.
_meta.numerator_is_snaps: Games with offensive snaps, NOT games with a stat line. A blocking TE, a receiver who ran routes and drew no targets, and a QB who handed off twice all record zero stats while playing, and counting stat lines put the median at 63%.
_meta.source: nflverse rosters (the denominator) x snap_counts, offensive snaps > 0 (the numerator)
